verdict.rationale: Square's only first-party rules capability in the evidence is a fraud-risk feature that lets sellers "set custom rules and alerts to manage risk" on payments. That is a narrow, risk-only form of event-triggered automation. Webhook event notifications are a developer building block for constructing automation, not a user-definable rules engine, so they earn no credit here. Missing for 10: a general-purpose rules or automation builder across Square events (orders, inventory, customers), documentation of which actions rules can trigger beyond alerts, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Get insights into payment fraud patterns, and set custom rules and alerts to manage risk.
